evals.prompt: Review this change to an existing, already-shipped endpoint: GET /api/orders currently returns `{ status: string }` for order status, and we want to change it to `{ status: number }` (an enum code) to save bandwidth.
evals.expected_output: Should flag this as a breaking change (field type change from string to number) that would break any existing client parsing the field as a string. Should recommend either a new API version, an additive new field (e.g. add `statusCode` alongside keeping `status` as string), or explicit client coordination - not approve the type change in place silently.
assertions: Identifies this as a breaking change
Explains specifically why (type change breaks existing client parsing)
Recommends versioning or an additive approach rather than in-place replacement
Does not approve the change without flagging the compatibility issue

evals.prompt: Our existing API uses `/v1/customer` (singular) for all resources and a `{ error: { code, message } }` error shape everywhere. Review this new endpoint proposal: `POST /createCustomerOrder` returning errors as `{ success: false, errorMessage: '...' }`.
evals.expected_output: Should flag both the naming convention mismatch (verb-in-path instead of resource+HTTP-method, and inconsistent with existing singular-noun convention - should point out the endpoint should look more like the existing pattern, e.g. POST /customer/{id}/order) and the error shape inconsistency (different shape than the rest of the API), citing brownfield consistency as the reason rather than abstract REST best practice alone.
assertions: Flags the verb-based endpoint naming as inconsistent with existing conventions
Flags the error response shape as inconsistent with the existing error format
Justifies findings via existing codebase convention (brownfield), not just generic REST theory
Proposes a concrete corrected form consistent with existing patterns
